main_body: Thatched hip-roof hut: a large thatch roof slope over a log wall with a recessed doorway and two round shields
top_band: Thatch roof slope, rows 7-55 (gold #9c7a30 with lighter #bc9a45 tile-row highlights), ending at an eave line at about rows 53-55. The wall below is much darker.
evidence: The roof is a large slope seen from above. Its outline widens in steps toward the eaves, so it reads as a hip roof, like the reference house roofs. Below the lighter eave row (about rows 53-55) the wall drops abruptly to dark brown log tones, so there is a clear step between roof and front face. The wall has its own shading, with vertical logs and a dark shadow under the eave. The door is inset, with a frame, a dark inner edge and a stone threshold. There are no receding isometric side faces. Roof and wall both follow the contract.

style.evidence: The thatch uses about 5 steps (dark band, mid, base, highlight), with a tile-row highlight pattern. The logs carry several browns, with a stone sill and shield details. Only 13% of dark edge pixels are neutral and the outlines lean brown, so they read as material tones. Flat-fill coverage is 2%. The median of 9 colours per tile is slightly below the references (11 and 18), and the 38 distinct colours is lower than both. The thatch rows repeat somewhat mechanically. It would still sit acceptably next to the references without looking like a sticker.
